description: Register for Zoom Speaker Julius Otieno Oyugi, PhD Professor, Department of Medical Microbiology at the University of Nairobi; Deputy Director of the University of Nairobi Institute of Tropical and Infectious Diseases Series Goals Global Partner Spotlights highlight the work of IGHS partners around the world, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. These sessions will provide a window into the priorities, challenges, and innovations of IGHS collaborators in-country. Speaker Biography Prof. Julius Otieno Oyugi is a Kenyan microbiologist and virologist with extensive experience in infectious disease research, laboratory science, academic leadership, and global health training. He is a Professor in the Department of Medical Microbiology at the University of Nairobi and serves as Deputy Director of the University of Nairobi Institute of Tropical and Infectious Diseases (UNITID). Prof. Oyugi received his PhD in Microbiology/Virology from the University of Manitoba, Canada, in 2008, following an MSc in Virology from John Moores University, Liverpool, United Kingdom and advanced training in Virology and Medical Laboratory Sciences in Kenya. His career spans more than two decades and includes research, teaching, laboratory management, and leadership roles at the University of Nairobi and international institutions. Prior to his current professorial role, Prof. Oyugi served as Senior Lecturer and Lecturer in the Department of Medical Microbiology at the University of Nairobi, as well as Laboratory Manager at UNITID. He has also contributed to international infectious disease capacity building as Training Coordinator for the CIHR International Infectious Disease and Global Health Training Program. Earlier in his career, he worked as a Research Technician with the Kenya AIDS Vaccine Initiative (KAVI). Prof. Oyugi has held leadership and academic appointments in both Kenya and Canada and has been involved in strengthening infectious disease research and laboratory capacity. He is a member of the Kenya Medical Laboratory Technicians and Technologists Board and has been affiliated with the American Society for Microbiology. Question? Please contact: IGHSConnect@ucsf.edu UCSF welcomes all participants to our events. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in this event because of a disability, please contact pilar.deer@ucsf.edu as soon as possible.

description: Dear colleagues, The Institute for Human Genetics, the Center for Advanced Technology and CoLabs invite you to the next talk in the Technology Seminar Series, presented by Novogene. Genomic and transcriptomic data tell you what a cell is capable of, but not what it is actually doing. This seminar covers how mass spectrometry based proteomics and metabolomics close that gap, and where they add the most value alongside sequencing. The speakers will walk through deep DIA proteomics, plasma and serum proteomics, phosphoproteomics and untargeted metabolomics, with realistic expectations for depth, throughput and turnaround, followed by a practical section on study design: sample types and input requirements, when to run proteomics in parallel with sequencing versus as a follow-up, and how the resulting layers are integrated. Speakers: Pierce Popson, Account Manager, Novogene; Anthony Tong, MS Product Manager, Novogene; Craig Marquis, Account Manager, Novogene Lunch is provided. Please RSVP so we can get an accurate headcount and accommodate dietary restrictions: https://humangenetics.ucsf.edu/lunch-and-learn-tech-seminar-series-novogene-0 As always, the seminar is free and open to all.

description: The first IVF baby is only 48 years old. In our generation, egg freezing went from science fiction to a standard tech company perk and yet almost nobody talks about the part that keeps people up at night: the money, the odds, and how to decide when the data is messy and the bill runs past $15k. This isn't medical advice, but an honest look at fertility as a financial decision when we all hope to have the families we want, but the dropping fertility rates look dire. I love chasing history, and will cover how health insurance evolved to leave fertility out, what the real success and cost numbers say, and a clear way to think about whether egg freezing is for you. For people thinking about freezing, donating eggs, family-planning, or those curious about the options they have for the careers they want to have, its a great way to understand the biggest life risk nobody sells an insurance plan for. I'm an early-stage founder building in fertility, and my background is in fintech. I led product teams at Robinhood and Intuit, and a core tenet of my life has been to help make complicated, high stakes money decisions simple enough for any normal person to actually make.

description: BCHSI Special Invited Seminar Topic: "Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Decision Making Across Modalities" Lunch Served 12:30 – 1:00 pm Seminar 1:10 – 2:00 pm Rock Hall Auditorium & by Zoom In place of the monthly BCHSI-wide Lab meeting, we will host Dr. Dvir Aran, who is currently a Visiting Scholar at UCSF - join us in welcoming him! FEATURED SPEAKER Dvir Aran, PhD, Associate Professor Faculty of Biology\Taub Faculty of Computer Science Technion -Israel Institute of Technology In this seminar, Dr. Aran will present two recent works that illustrate how artificial intelligence can democratize clinical decision-making. The first develops a deep learning model that predicts breast cancer recurrence risk directly from histopathology images, offering a scalable alternative to costly molecular assays. The second introduces a conversational, multi-agent AI system for neurological diagnosis, which achieves higher accuracy than physicians while reducing costs. Together, these studies show how AI can extend expert-level decision support to settings with limited resources, advancing both equity and efficiency in clinical care. description: Session Overview This hands-on workshop focuses on how to best start basic literature searching using a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools. Discussion will cover questions to consider that guide whether an AI tool, such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Consensus, and Perplexity, can be helpful in the literature searching process. Participants will practice searching a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools to critique the results. There will be time for questions and discussion throughout the workshop. Learning Objectives Determine where AI tools may fit into the literature searching workflowCompare and contrast answers provided by databases vs. AI toolsCreate prompts to optimize AI tool answers to compliment database searchingRegister to receive the Zoom link and password. About the series This session is part of the AI in your Toolkit: Critical approaches to using AI in your work workshop series. The next workshop is October 8, at 11 a.m. - 12:30 p.m. and covers AI Tools for Review Projects. About the instructor Josephine Tan, MLIS, is an Education and Research Librarian.
